title: Enums, records and custom exceptions

notes: Each Light constant carries its own seconds.
The switch covers every constant; add a new one and the compiler complains.
Visit is a record; the compact constructor only checks the day.
NoSlotException extends Exception, so it is checked.
book() must declare `throws NoSlotException`, and main must catch it.

exercises.title: Crop enum
exercises.prompt: Finish enum Crop with constants MAIZE("Maize", 55), BEANS("Beans", 120), RICE("Rice", 140), SORGHUM("Sorghum", 45) (label, price per kg in KSh). getLabel(), getPricePerKg(), value(double kg) = kg × price. static fromName(String name) turns " rice " or "Rice" into RICE and throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown names. isGrain() is true for maize, rice and sorghum (use a switch).

tests.name: unknown crop
tests.hint_if_fail: Crop.valueOf already throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown names.

hints: Constants with arguments: MAIZE("Maize", 55), ... ; then private final fields and a constructor Crop(String label, int pricePerKg).
isGrain: return switch (this) { case BEANS -> false; default -> true; };

exercises.title: Sensor readings as records
exercises.prompt: Give record Reading(String sensor, double litres, int hour) a compact constructor that throws IllegalArgumentException for a blank sensor name, negative litres, or an hour outside 0-23, and a method isNight() (hour before 6 or from 20 on). In Readings write static double totalFor(List<Reading> rs, String sensor) and static int nightCount(List<Reading> rs).

tests.call: Readings.totalFor(java.util.List.of(new Reading("a", 10, 1), new Reading("b", 5, 2), new Reading("a", 2.5, 3)), "a")
Readings.nightCount(java.util.List.of(new Reading("a", 10, 1), new Reading("b", 5, 12), new Reading("a", 2.5, 20)))

hints: Compact constructor: record Reading(...) { Reading { if (...) throw ...; } ... }
Use the record's accessors: r.sensor(), r.litres(), r.hour().
if (sensor == null || sensor.isBlank() || litres < 0 || hour < 0 || hour > 23) throw new IllegalArgumentException(...);

exercises.title: Pharmacy exceptions
exercises.prompt: OutOfStockException is CHECKED (extends Exception): its message is "Only 3 Amoxicillin left, wanted 5" and getWanted()/getAvailable() return the numbers. InvalidQuantityException is UNCHECKED (extends RuntimeException). In Pharmacy: addStock(item, qty) throws InvalidQuantityException if qty <= 0; stockOf(item) (0 if unknown); dispense(item, qty) throws InvalidQuantityException if qty <= 0, OutOfStockException if there isn't enough, otherwise takes the stock and returns what is left. static tryDispense(Pharmacy p, String item, int qty) returns "OK, 6 left" or the OutOfStockException's message.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Pharmacy p = new Pharmacy(); p.addStock("ORS", 10); return Pharmacy.tryDispense(p, "ORS", 4); }).get()
((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Pharmacy p = new Pharmacy(); p.addStock("Amoxicillin", 3); return Pharmacy.tryDispense(p, "Amoxicillin", 5) + " / " + p.stockOf("Amoxicillin"); }).get()
tests.name: not enough: nothing taken

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Pharmacy p = new Pharmacy(); p.addStock("ORS", 0); return "no error"; }).get()
tests.name: adding 0

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Pharmacy p = new Pharmacy(); p.addStock("ORS", 10); try { p.dispense("ORS", 99); return "no error"; } catch (OutOfStockException e) { return e.getWanted() + " " + e.getAvailable(); } }).get()
tests.name: exception carries the numbers

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Pharmacy p = new Pharmacy(); p.addStock("ORS", 10); try { p.dispense("ORS", -1); return "no error"; } catch (OutOfStockException e) { return "wrong exception"; } }).get()
tests.name: negative dispense

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { Pharmacy p = new Pharmacy(); return Pharmacy.tryDispense(p, "Zinc", 1); }).get()
tests.name: never stocked

hints: OutOfStockException: store wanted and available in fields; call super("Only " + available + " " + item + " left, wanted " + wanted);
dispense: int have = stockOf(item); if (qty > have) throw new OutOfStockException(item, qty, have);
tryDispense: try { return "OK, " + p.dispense(item, qty) + " left"; } catch (OutOfStockException e) { return e.getMessage(); }

quiz.q: Why an enum instead of Strings for crop types?
choices: Only the listed values exist, so typos can't sneak in
quiz.why: The compiler only accepts real constants.
valueOf only knows the declared constants.

quiz.q: A record gives you for free…
Your exception extends Exception. What does the compiler demand?
choices: Methods that throw it declare `throws`, and callers catch or declare it

quiz.q: Best kind for 'quantity was negative' (a caller's bug)?
quiz.why: Programming mistakes are unchecked; plan-for situations are checked.

cards.q: List all constants of an enum?

cards.a: record R(int x) { R { if (x < 0) throw ...; } }  Just the checks.
extends Exception: must catch/declare. extends RuntimeException: no need.

explain: Explain when you'd make an exception checked and when unchecked, using a clinic or game example you make up.
